subject: Art & Design
title: Color Harmony in Interior Design
description: One-minute skill: Color Harmony in Interior Design.

hook.text: Paint one wall of a small room dark. Suddenly the room feels larger. Color reshapes space.

buildup.text: Interior designers use the 60-30-10 rule: dominant color, secondary color, accent color.

discovery.text: Light colors open up small rooms. Dark colors make large rooms feel intimate and cozy.

twist.text: Natural light shifts throughout the day. A perfect wall color at noon can look terrible at dusk.

climax.text: Always test paint samples on the actual wall — screens and swatches lie under different lighting.

punchline.text: Don't pick colors from a screen. Pick them from the room.

quiz.question: What is the 60-30-10 rule in interior design?
options: Ratio of dominant, secondary, and accent color usage
How many minutes to spend choosing paint

details.summary: Interior color theory applies the same principles as graphic design — complementary, analogous, and monochromatic schemes — but accounts for architectural light, texture, and the fact that people live inside the design for hours daily. A color that energizes in a poster can exhaust in a bedroom.
details.whyItMatters: Interior color choices affect daily mood and well-being for years, not seconds. A poorly chosen wall color can make a room feel smaller, more anxious, or less restful.
takeaways: Same color schemes as graphic design but adjusted for living spaces
Architectural light and texture alter color perception
Poor color choices affect daily mood and well-being for years

faq.question: Why do paint colors look different on the wall than the swatch?
faq.answer: Scale, lighting, and surrounding colors all change perception. A small swatch under store fluorescents looks different covering an entire wall under natural light. Large areas of color appear more saturated.

faq.question: What ceiling color makes a room feel bigger?
faq.answer: White or light ceilings make rooms feel taller because the eye reads lighter surfaces as farther away. Painting walls slightly darker than the ceiling increases this effect. Conversely, dark ceilings create intimacy in large spaces.
